countries: US (New York City, New Haven CT, Los Angeles)
_meta.conventions: Each figure is {value, unit, currency?, basis, source, date, sourceType, confirmed}. sourceType 'primary' = the authority's or maker's/retailer's own page or dataset; 'secondary' = press, compiler, cost-guide or consumer-organization article. confirmed:true means the figure was read on the page or in the downloaded file itself; confirmed:false means it was seen only in a search-engine snippet or summary (the page was blocked by a bot wall, 403 or Cloudflare). value:null means no published figure was found. Retail prices are shelf prices on the date seen and move with promotions; Mexican retailers in particular show deep 'sale' prices against inflated 'regular' prices.
_meta.notOwnedByThisFile: Share of homes with each appliance and household electricity prices per kWh are already in the game and were not researched.

NYC.basis: 1 RCNY §101-14, Table 1 (one- and two-family dwellings): a packaged air-conditioning unit not exceeding 5 tons rated capacity, installed in an existing building including in existing windows or sleeves, and not part of an alteration that otherwise needs a permit, is exempt. Table 2 (all buildings): the same exemption at 3 tons or less. The DOB page says a permit is generally not needed for a common window unit unless it exceeds three tons / 36,000 BTU/h.

A split system or central AC is not a 'packaged' unit, so the exemption does not cover it; installer and trade sources say a mini-split with an exterior condenser, wall penetrations or new circuits needs a DOB filing. No DOB page stating this for split systems was read.

LA.basis: LADBS Information Bulletin P/GI 2020-003 lists as express permits (no plan check) comfort cooling installations under 500,000 Btu/h aggregate and 'addition of air conditioning equipment having a rating of 5 tons or less'. LADBS's mechanical HVAC page says a mechanical permit is required for installing or modifying heating or cooling systems.

typicalSize.basis: Angi size bands used in its cost table; HomeGuide says the most common 2-car garages are 400-576 sq ft; Angi elsewhere gives 18 x 20 ft (360 sq ft) as the average two-car size. No ICC or other code sets a garage size.

NYC.value: permit required for a garage; sheds exempt only up to 120 sq ft
NYC.basis: 1 RCNY §101-14 exempts only temporary portable sheds accessory to a one- or two-family dwelling (max 120 sq ft, 7'6" high, 3 ft from lot lines, one per lot); a garage is not on the exempt list, so it needs a DOB filing. Zoning: accessory parking in a required rear yard of a one- or two-family home is limited to a detached building no more than 10 ft high (per Zoning Resolution, seen only in a snippet).

LA.basis: California/LA practice: one-story detached accessory buildings used as tool/storage sheds, playhouses and similar are permit-exempt only up to 120 sq ft; garages need a building permit. Not read on an LADBS page.

England.basis: Planning Portal: outbuildings and garages single storey, max eaves 2.5 m, max overall height 4 m with a dual-pitched roof or 3 m otherwise; max 2.5 m if within 2 m of a boundary; not forward of the principal elevation; no more than half the land around the original house covered; in National Parks, AONBs, the Broads and World Heritage Sites, buildings more than 20 m from the house limited to 10 m2. Flats and maisonettes have no such rights; Article 4 directions and conservation areas can remove them (common in London).

Ireland.unit: m2, exempt total for garages, sheds and similar within a house's curtilage
Ireland.basis: Planning and Development Regulations 2001 (S.I. 600/2001), Schedule 2 Part 1, Class 3: not forward of the front wall; total with earlier such structures not over 25 m2; leaves at least 25 m2 private open space; finishes match the house when at the side; height max 4 m with a tiled or slated pitched roof, else 3 m; no habitation. S.I. 340/2026 (in force 27 July 2026) inserted a new Class 3A (detached dwelling of 32-45 m2 in a rear garden) and did not change Class 3; structures under Class 3 count toward Class 3A's 45 m2.

England_ManualForStreets.basis: Manual for Streets para 8.3.39-8.3.41: garages are not always used for parking; surveys found 44% (various English sites), 36% (Waterside Park, Kent) and 45% (Oxfordshire) of garages used for parking; car ports should count; whether garages count fully depends on other parking, cycle and storage provision and garage size (6 m x 3 m minimum widely recommended).

London.basis: The London Plan 2021 (Policy T6.1) sets maximum residential parking and no rule on whether a garage counts was found; borough SPDs were not readable. Many English councils (e.g. Basingstoke, Leicestershire) count a garage only if it meets 6 m x 3 m internal.

Dublin.basis: Dublin City Development Plan 2022-2028, Appendix 5: maximum parking for houses/apartments 0.5 per dwelling (Zone 1) and 1 per dwelling (Zones 2-3); a car in a front garden needs 3 m x 5 m; mews parking 'will be in off-street garages, forecourts or courtyards'. No statement on whether a garage counts as a space.

uncertain: Most retailer prices (Harvey Norman Ireland, Home Depot Canada, Home Depot México, Liverpool, Coppel, Currys, Lowe's, Home Depot US) were seen only in search snippets, because those sites block automated reads with a 403 or Cloudflare challenge. They are marked confirmed:false, and some model numbers could not be captured.
No US retailer best-seller median price was obtained for any appliance, and there is no US electric-range price at all: Consumer Reports' range guide carries no prices.
Home Depot's and Lowe's current published installation fees could not be read directly. The US dishwasher install figures come from compilers or search summaries.
No official per-appliance annual kWh was found for the UK, Ireland or Mexico. The UK kWh are derived from Which? running costs at 26.32p/kWh, and Ireland has nothing.
The Canadian kWh (NRCan) come from search snippets only, since oee.nrcan.gc.ca refused connections, and they describe new units shipped in 2020, not the stock average.

The DOE FEMP central-AC and room-AC kWh use federal-facility operating hours, not household use. The household figure is RECS 2020's all-types AC average: 2,318 kWh nationally, 1,483 in the Middle Atlantic division and 1,514 in the Pacific division.
EIA RECS 2024 end-use (kWh) tables are not yet published; EIA says spring 2027. All US kWh are RECS 2020.
Lifespans rest on the 2007 NAHB study. No newer NAHB edition was found, and it does not separate room AC from central AC.

Mexico has no electric-dryer price, no window-AC price and no central-AC price. Electric ranges are rare there; the stove price is for an LP-gas model. Profeco's Quién es Quién en los Precios appliance data was not read.
The Consumer Reports member median of $855 for a dishwasher was seen only in a search summary.
The Which? dishwasher price article is from 2019. No 2026 Which? dishwasher price range was readable.
The ENIGH 2024 furniture-only line (muebles) was not extracted. Only the combined household-goods-and-cleaning rubro is recorded.

No authoritative cost to furnish a whole home or one-bedroom apartment was found: no IKEA package price and no consumer-organization estimate. Only a low-authority blog range is recorded, marked unconfirmed.
No garage-build cost was found for Ireland, Canada or Mexico.
The LA garage permit rule (sheds exempt to 120 sq ft; garages need a permit) was not read on an LADBS page.
Whether a garage counts as a parking space was not found stated in the London Plan or any London borough SPD, or in the Dublin City Development Plan.
Whether NYC DOB requires a permit for a mini-split or central AC was inferred from the packaged-unit exemption not covering split systems. No DOB page stating it was read.
